title: OpenAI's Secret: Compute is King, Not Customers! #shorts
description: The conventional wisdom is spending too much, too soon. OpenAI triples compute annually, finding revenue directly correlates. Their only constraint? Silicon, not customers. #OpenAI #TechGrowth #AICapital #ComputePower #BusinessStrategy
transcript: The conventional wisdom is spending too much, too soon. OpenAI triples compute annually, finding revenue directly correlates. Their only constraint? Silicon, not customers. #OpenAI #TechGrowth #AICapital #ComputePower #BusinessStrategy

top_comments.author: @JordanJordi-d4d
top_comments.text: Silicon as the constraint rather than demand makes sense. Been hitting this in deployment. Teams with multi-year GPU allocations live in a completely different world from everyone on spot access.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Yeah that gap is real — when some teams have GPUs locked in for years and everyone else is fighting for scraps on spot, it stops being about demand and starts being about who can actually ship. It turns deployment into a lottery instead of a plan. How are you handling it on your side when you don’t have that long-term allocation?

top_comments.author: @CircuitSage-d5e
top_comments.text: Stop chasing petaflops; start focusing on performance per dollar. Revenue tracking supply is consumption, not demand.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Exactly — raw petaflops look good in a slide but they don’t pay bills, efficiency and cost do. If revenue is just tracking whatever supply is available, then we’re measuring access, not real need. How are you balancing performance per dollar in your own deployments right now?
